what_happened: the per-set supplement was pointed at the WRONG baseline and it was caught before it produced a number, by a canvas mismatch that had no business existing.
the_symptom: the donor arm (the control's own configuration, rebuilt from raws under today's tree) delivered per-set stacks of 4907x3598 / 4902x3633 / 4903x3675 against the control's 4907x3598 / 4894x3752 / 4900x3719. Set-01 matched; set-02 and set-03 did not. That is impossible if the inputs and the code are the same, so one of them was not.
the_inputs_were_the_same_and_this_was_me: all 13 donor members reproduce the control's members EXACTLY — 0 differing pixels of 893,212,122 across the three sets (set-01 0/346,610,448; set-02 0/273,597,216; set-03 0/273,004,458). So the members are not the difference and the per-set COMPOSE is.
the_cause_read_off_the_two_builds_own_ge: both builds leave their final.ssf on disk, so no inference was needed. Control: `register s -2pass` then `seqapplyreg s -framing=min -prefix=r_`. Donor: `register s -2pass -transf=homography`, `setref s 1`, `seqapplyreg s -framing=min -prefix=r_ -interp=lanczos4`. The `setref s 1` anchor landed in commit 739c626 at 08-11 14:42; the control's per-set stacks were built that morning at 09:22 / 10:37 / 11:31. They therefore carry the OLD UNPINNED auto-pick reference, and the pin changes which member the canvas is based on.
why_set_01_matched: coincidence, and a dangerous one — the unpinned auto-pick happened to land on member 1 there, which is what `setref s 1` pins it to. A one-set check would have concluded the two builds agree.
consequence_for_the_experiment: the control's per-set stacks are NOT a one-knob baseline for an arm built by today's code: arm A vs stack_set-0X_full would have differed by the background step AND by the compose reference. The per-set supplement is rebased onto the DONOR per-set stack (stack_set-0X_l1ctrl) — identical members, identical code, differing from arm A by the background step alone — and ALL THREE per-set surfaces (baseline, on-stack level, per-frame arm) now sit on it, so retained_A and the on-stack retained share a denominator exactly.
what_is_kept_rather_than_discarded: the earlier per-set on-stack readings against the control surface (starlight_ctrl.json / starlight_subsky1.json in each set's starlight_work) stay valid ON THEIR OWN TERMS — each is paired against its own baseline, so it is internally one-knob — and they become an independent second measurement of the on-stack level on a differently-anchored surface. They are not deleted and not used as arm A's baseline.
the_union_is_unaffected: the union is composed by run_undistort_compose.sh, which the setref change did not touch, and the arm unions use the same default reference (member 1) as the control union — verified from the control's own compose-gate record, reference_member s_00001. The only code delta on that path since the control union is the explicit `-interp=lanczos4`, which this session's member-level rebuild proves is a no-op by re-execution (0 differing pixels).
a_claim_in_the_tree_that_does_not_hold_a: FIRST VERSION OF THIS FIELD WAS WRONG AND THE ERROR IS INSTRUCTIVE. It said commit 739c626's message describes the pin as `verified bit-identical`. It does not. Read directly, that message says: 'Verified: pinned recompose of aug06/SET-01 is bit-identical to the shipped stack (isub all-nil x3 channels, x1.01 control)'. It names the set AND carries a non-vacuous control. The claim is honest and correctly scoped. What dropped the scope is prompts/REPORT.md's done-ledger — 'per-set compose reference pinned (verified bit-identical)', no set named — i.e. a SUMMARY over-claiming relative to the evidence it was summarising. The measurement below is unaffected; only the attribution was.
how_i_made_that_error_which_is_the_same_: I read the ledger line and attributed it to the commit without opening the commit. That is trusting a summary over its primary source — the identical move to trusting 'same frames' over 'same code', which is the finding this record exists to state. Caught by the audit session, which read the commit. Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because a correction record that itself contains an unverified attribution would be the worst possible version of this file.
what_actually_does_not_hold: the DONE-LEDGER's unqualified summary, not the commit. On aug06 the pin moves the delivered canvas on set-02 (4894x3752 -> 4902x3633) and set-03 (4900x3719 -> 4903x3675) with identical members; set-01 IS bit-identical, and its unpinned auto-pick already selected member 1, which is what the pin forces — so a one-set verification could not distinguish 'no effect' from 'no effect HERE'. The pin itself is correct and wanted: it is the fix for the reference lottery.
how_it_was_caught: not by a guard. By reading two header canvases that should have been equal, and refusing to proceed until the difference was explained. The check that made it decisive was cheap and tool-free: diff the two builds' own generated .ssf files, which both routes leave on disk.
